summary: A set of flow diagrams, dated August 1969, describing the logic of the interface between an IMP and its host computer, including steps for messages moving from the IMP to the host. It documents the hardware-level interface logic as drawn in diagrams.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 12 presents flow diagrams for messages moving between an ARPANET host and its IMP. The diagrams show the sequence of hardware operations in each direction.

questions: how did the imp host interface hardware work
what do rfc 12 flow diagrams show
how did messages move from an imp to a host
subtitle: Flow diagrams of the hardware sequence for messages between an IMP and a host.

tldr.problem: Readers needed to follow the order of hardware operations at the IMP-host interface.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 12 reproduces flow diagrams from Appendix B of BBN Report No. 1822, covering messages in both directions.
tldr.outcome: The document is a visual record of interface logic, not a general explanation of the ARPANET.

today: The unit metadata records the status of RFC 12 as Unknown and lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It remains a document of IMP-host interface flow diagrams dated 26 August 1969.

sections.title: Purpose of the Flow Diagrams
sections.content:
The document says its diagrams were extracted from the logic diagrams in Appendix B of BBN Report No. 1822. They show the logical sequence of hardware operations within the IMP-host interface.

The names in the diagram blocks correspond to logic elements in that appendix. The document provides diagrams rather than a longer prose description.
sections.plainLanguage: The diagrams turn interface logic into a sequence of steps. Their labels refer to elements in the source report's logic diagrams.

sections.title: A Message from the IMP to the Host
sections.content:
The input flow clears several flags and a counter, then signals readiness for an IMP bit. It waits for the bit and checks whether the IMP is ready; the diagram sets an error flag if the IMP is not ready.

The flow checks for the last bit, shifts data and counts it. When a word is complete, it requests that the host take the data, then continues or ends according to the diagram's last-message and padding checks.
sections.plainLanguage: For an incoming message, the interface waits for data, checks readiness and moves the data into the host. It repeats until the diagram's end conditions are met.

sections.title: A Message from the Host to the IMP
sections.content:
The output flow requests a data word from the host and waits for the word's strobe. It loads the word into a shift register, then coordinates the transfer using the RFNBIT signal and a counter.

The diagram checks the word length and whether the current word is the last. It marks the last bit where needed, pushes the shift register and repeats until the message ends.
sections.plainLanguage: For an outgoing message, the interface requests a word, loads it and sends it through the shift register. It marks the final word and ends the transfer when the diagram's conditions are satisfied.
